subject: Follow-up: POC success criteria & evaluation approach for Clearpoint Health
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Gupta <anna.gupta@clearpointhealth.com>, Ben Chavez <ben.chavez@clearpointhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC success sprint charter

Hi Anna / Ben — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight charter so we can get to a concrete kickoff next week. Please confirm or edit below.

Goal: validate Redwood's inference for discharge-summary generation at Clearpoint (phase 1) with a measurable success gate and low-risk rollout path.

Proposed success criteria (acceptance thresholds):
- Accuracy / fidelity: > 85% on clinician-labeled holdout (exact-match on key fields: diagnosis, meds, follow-ups)
- Hallucination rate: < 3% on random sample of 500 generated summaries
- Latency: median generation time < 600 ms for 512-token requests
- Cost sensitivity: per-request token cost under $X (we'll baseline after first day)
- Human review delta: reviewer edit-time <= 30% of baseline manual composition time

Eval approach options (please indicate preference):
A) Offline batch evaluation (holdout dataset): Redwood runs batch inference on de-identified examples you provide, returns scoring matrix and error annotations. Low-risk, controlled, faster scoring but synthetic for live edge-cases.
B) Shadow (online) mode: Redwood routes a % of traffic in parallel (no user-visible changes), we compare outputs to baseline in production. Best for safety/real-world distribution but requires integration and short warmup.

Suggested timeline:
- Day 0: kickoff + signing of mutual action plan (MAP) and data access checklist
- Day 1–3: data exchange and de-id verification; Redwood runs initial offline pass
- Day 4–10: iteration on model/config; run offline scoring and quick manual spot checks
- Day 11–14: optional shadow run (if agreed) + final acceptance report

Owners:
- Redwood AE / program lead: Dylan Brooks (owner of MAP + timeline)
- Redwood CSM: Marissa Cole (onboarding, ops, and success gating)
- Solutions + integration: Rishi Malhotra (dataset/infra, shadow integration)
- Clearpoint: Anna (ML/PII ownership), Ben (procurement / timeline approvals)

Attachments: POC-charter-draft.pdf (draft charter, 2 pages); evaluation-scoring-matrix.xlsx (scoring template).

Next steps / asks for Clearpoint: confirm preferred eval approach (A or B), confirm availability for 30-minute kickoff (propose Mon Nov 17 or Tue Nov 18), and share a sample of 200 de-identified notes for the offline run if you pick option A.

Thanks — I can adapt the charter based on your feedback and loop in Product if we need a custom metric.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0192 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
From: Anna Gupta <anna.gupta@clearpointhealth.com>

Cc: Ben Chavez <ben.chavez@clearpointhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 17:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC success sprint charter

Dylan — thanks for the clear summary. We prefer option A (offline batch) to start: we need to validate on de-identified historical notes first. A couple of clarifications / asks from our side: 

- Data & privacy: Can Redwood accept S3 with server-side encryption? We'll need a short data handling addendum and confirmation of SOC2 in-scope controls for log retention.
- Scoring: we care about clinical safety categories more than exact-match for free-text fields. Can the scoring matrix include a clinical-severity error tag (Minor / Major / Safety-critical)?
- Timeline: Mon Nov 17 works for a kickoff, but procurement sign-off may slip; Ben is looping procurement in.

We'll send an initial 200-note de-identified set by EOD Friday if the S3 transfer approach is acceptable.

— Anna
Anna Gupta
Head of Applied ML | Clearpoint Health
anna.gupta@clearpointhealth.com

Thanks Anna — S3 with SSE is fine; we'll send a short data handling addendum and a SOC2 evidence packet (summary + auditor contact) prior to the kickoff.

Rishi and I will prepare a modified scoring matrix that adds the clinical-severity error tag you requested (Minor / Major / Safety-critical). Rishi: can you confirm whether we can score safety-critical errors automatically or if we should mark for manual review?

Action items I will own:
- Share data handling addendum (today)
- Upload initial scoring matrix template (including severity tags) to Drive and share link
- Tentatively schedule kickoff for Mon Nov 17, 10:00–10:30 PT (Dylan, please confirm)

On Fri, Nov 14, 2025 at 08:07 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi and I will prepare a modified scoring matrix that adds the clinical-severity error tag you requested (Minor / Major / Safety-critical). Rishi: can you confirm whether we can score safety-critical errors automatically or if we should mark for manual review?

Anna / Marissa — quick note: for safety-critical categories we'll flag candidates automatically but require a manual adjudication pass for final labeling during this POC. For the offline run we can provide an annotation UI export (CSV with line-level diffs and candidate tags) so your clinical reviewers can adjudicate quickly. That approach keeps automated triage but ensures human-in-the-loop for the safety gate.

I'll upload the adjusted scoring matrix (with new columns) and a short runbook for the offline execution to the Drive link Marissa shares.

Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
